dial.summary: BTC Accumulation thesis intact on Aug 31 with 7 of 8 indicators supportive: Global M2 at $103.4T rising on a 4-week basis, ISM PMI at 55.6% (July; August 2026 ISM releases tomorrow Sep 1), real yields at 2.34% and falling, 2s10s steepening to +39bps, stablecoin dominance declining to 11.29% and BTC.D holding at 57.96%—DXY at 99.65 remains in the neutral band and sliding, maintaining a constructive backdrop for risk assets heading into the Sep 1 ISM / Sep 4 NFP / Sep 10 ECB / Sep 11 CPI data cluster before FOMC Sep 16.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; ~6-week reporting lag on full aggregate); US M2 for July 2026 confirmed at $23.22T (record high, +$102.8B MoM, 29th consecutive monthly increase, +6.11% YoY, per BEA Aug 29 release); global M2 rising ~$0.7T over 4 weeks from ~$102.7T (late June 2026) to $103.4T (July 2026); no YoY contraction from any major central bank; 4-week uptrend confirmed; August global aggregate not yet available (6-week lag); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); September FOMC (Sep 16) is the next key catalyst for global liquidity trajectory.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3) remains the most recent official reading—August 2026 ISM data releases tomorrow, September 1 at 10:00 AM ET; S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI flash for August 2026 came in at 53.2 (preliminary, easing from 53.9 in July), suggesting some softening ahead of the official ISM print; sub-indexes for July: New Orders 56.7%, Production 58.5%, Employment 52.8%, Prices Paid 71.1%; highest reading since May 2022; 4-week trend up (June 53.3% → July 55.6%, +2.3pp); status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds of <48 falling or >62 not met); a September 1 reading below 50 alongside any hawkish policy signal would trigger a Risk Off reassessment ahead of FOMC Sep 16.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.65 on August 30–31, 2026 (most recent available; Aug 28 Friday close ~99.67, Aug 30 forex close 99.6509; Aug 31 markets open); 4-week trend down: DXY peaked near 100.8–101.0 in late July 2026 and has declined to ~99.65, a ~1.1% decline over 4 weeks, above the 0.5% flat threshold; structural dollar weakness driven by US Treasury buyback program and rate-cut expectations ahead of FOMC Sep 16; status neutral (ICE DXY at 99.65 within 97.5–100 neutral band); Sep 1 ISM and Sep 4 NFP are next decisive inputs—a dovish macro outcome cluster accelerates DXY toward or below 97.5 (supportive territory).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 at 2.34% as of August 27, 2026 (H.15; most recent FRED observation; data for Aug 28 had not yet appeared in FRED as of Aug 31 AM); 4-week trend down: ~2.43% (July 28, 2026) → 2.34% (Aug 27) = −9bps, a confirmed falling trend; status supportive (falling trend satisfies the supportive condition per rule); the headwind rule requires both rising AND above 2%—the above-2% criterion is met, but the falling trend dominates status scoring; inflation (PCE) at 3.7% YoY (July 2026, released Aug 26) maintains elevated real yields in absolute terms, but the 4-week downtrend is the operative status driver; Sep 11 CPI and Sep 16 FOMC rate decision are the next key compression catalysts.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 28, 2026 H.15 close: 10Y yield 4.73%, 2Y yield 4.34% (confirmed per Treasury Yields Snapshot Aug 28); spread = +39bps (+0.39%); markets closed Aug 29–30 weekend, Aug 31 data not yet on FRED; 4-week steepening: ~+35bps (late July 2026) → +39bps (Aug 28) = +4bps steepening over 4 weeks; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening direction intact); upcoming catalysts: NFP (Sep 4), ECB (Sep 10), CPI (Sep 11), and FOMC (Sep 16) are the next curve-shaping inputs.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,730,912M (~$6.73T) for week ending August 26, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 27); unchanged from prior run; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (late July / early August) → $6.73T (Aug 26) = ~+$31B (+0.5%), within the flat threshold; minor week-over-week dip from $6.745T (Aug 19) to $6.731T (Aug 26) = −$14B reflects routine measured QT operations; balance sheet holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau with no aggressive QT signal and no overnight rate spike; status supportive (holding flat; QT pace stable); next H.4.1 release due Sep 3.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate held at approximately −0.0048% (MacroMicro aggregate; prior observation Aug 28–30, 2026); CoinGlass and other real-time aggregators remain blocked by egress proxy this run—value held from prior run per sourcing rules; BTC spot at ~$76,930 on Aug 31 (down from $80,294 on Aug 28 and $77,844 on Aug 29), indicating modest deleveraging; funding likely near zero or slightly negative consistent with the spot pullback and short-side pressure, remaining well below the +0.04%/8h overheating headwind threshold; 30-day trend flat: near zero throughout August; status supportive (near-zero funding, no long-side overextension signal). (Value held from prior run; BTC Funding Rates flagged as skipped this cycle—CoinGlass proxy-blocked.)

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$305B (CoinGecko Aug 31, 2026); total crypto market cap $2.71T; stablecoin dominance 11.29% (updated from 11.26% Aug 30); BTC.D 57.96% (firm, above 55% alt-rotation trigger threshold; BTC at ~$76,930 on Aug 31); 30-day trend down: confirmed—from ~13–14% in late July 2026 to 11.29% today; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition—dominance rising while TOTAL also rises—does not apply as total crypto cap is broadly flat/down on the day); BTC.D holding above 55% keeps Alt Rotation signal un-triggered.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM releases the August 2026 Manufacturing PMI Report on Business at 10:00 AM ET—first post-Jackson Hole official activity read; July 2026 ISM at 55.6% (highest since May 2022); S&P Global Manufacturing PMI flash for August came in at 53.2, suggesting potential softening; a sustained expansion above 50 reinforces risk asset positioning; a collapse below 50 alongside any hawkish signal would trigger a Risk Off reassessment ahead of FOMC September 16.

upcoming.title: ADP National Employment Report (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ADP releases the August 2026 National Employment Report at 8:15 AM ET—private sector employment proxy arriving two days before the official NFP (September 4); July ADP showed +44,000 private-sector jobs; a second weak reading reinforces the July NFP shock (−23K) and bolsters the rate-cut case heading into FOMC Sep 16; a strong rebound toward +100K+ would complicate the dovish narrative.

upcoming.title: Fed Beige Book (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Beige Book released at 2:00 PM ET, two weeks ahead of the FOMC meeting on September 16—qualitative snapshot of regional economic conditions across all 12 Fed districts; labor market health, inflation pressures, and credit conditions will be scrutinised for signals on the pace of easing; a broadly cooling Beige Book reinforces the dovish case, while stubborn price or wage pressures could temper rate-cut expectations into the September decision.

upcoming.title: ISM Services PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM releases the August 2026 Non-Manufacturing PMI at 10:00 AM ET—services sector counterpart to manufacturing ISM; services represent ~80% of US GDP; released one business day ahead of the August NFP report (September 4); a post-Jackson Hole services expansion reinforces the soft-landing narrative ahead of FOMC September 16.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 29, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending August 29—first post-Jackson Hole labor read; sets early framing ahead of the August NFP report (September 4) and FOMC September 16; a spike above 220K reinforces the case for a cut; a stable-to-declining read keeps the policy debate open heading into NFP.

upcoming.title: Nonfarm Payrolls (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—the second-to-last major data point before FOMC September 16 (after CPI Sep 11); July 2026 NFP shocked at −23K (vs +79K forecast), ADP July +44K; a further contraction would strongly argue for a rate cut and likely push DXY toward or below 97.5 (supportive for risk assets); a rebound toward +100K+ would complicate the dovish narrative; NFP and CPI Sep 11 form the final data trifecta shaping the September FOMC decision.
